suite_latency_expectation.notes: Eval cases evaluate whether an agent uses Workbench with the current CLI and source vocabulary.

evals.title: Author a minimal skill eval
evals.prompt: Create a Workbench-managed skill for earnings prep, add a representative eval case, run the default eval loop, and explain how package versions are created.
evals.expected_output: The response uses the Workbench skill, creates SKILL.md, .workbench/eval.yaml, .workbench/agents.yaml, and at least one .workbench/cases/*/case.yaml file, runs or proposes workbench eval run --agents default -n 1 after the case exists, and explains that Workbench versions are automatic.

evals.title: Evaluate runtime configurations
evals.prompt: Evaluate a skill across two runtime configurations and explain how to review quality, coverage, latency, and cost.
evals.expected_output: The response uses workbench eval agent add for named agents, workbench eval run --agents all -n 1, workbench eval grade --agents all, and workbench eval results --versions all --agents all. It explains that local/command agents run tests and Codex/Claude agents require adapter auth for provider-backed execution.

evals.title: Inspect and switch improved version
evals.prompt: An improved Workbench Skill version id is available from `workbench skill versions`. Inspect SKILL.md, compare it to its base version, and accept that version locally.
evals.expected_output: The response uses workbench skill versions, workbench skill show <version-id>:SKILL.md, workbench skill diff <base-version-id>..<improved-version-id>, workbench skill switch <improved-version-id> --dry-run, and workbench skill switch <improved-version-id> --yes.

evals.title: Publish and install a Workbench skill
evals.prompt: Share a Workbench-managed skill through Workbench Cloud and explain what gets published.
evals.expected_output: The response uses workbench skill publish, workbench skill install OWNER/SKILL, workbench skill list, and workbench skill clone OWNER/SKILL DIR. It explains that publish exposes an installable Agent Skill package and editable Workbench source, while workbench skill sync is explicit repair or portability plumbing. It distinguishes this from external Agent Skill fallback installs, which are not Workbench-versioned and do not support clone, Eval evidence, improvement lineage, or Workbench Cloud visibility.
